body: Hm, I wonder if this could ever work... anyway, I'll take a look next Monday.
@mkouba maybe we should fill the `timestampSet.watchedFileTimestamps` with the resources matching the predicate at startup.

So I looked into the code and it worked in my test by coincidence :facepalm:. A `HotDeploymentWatchedFileBuildItem` with a predicate is only considered when a new file is created. In my test this solved the problem with a new template added to the app because subsequent restarts were handled by the location-based `HotDeploymentWatchedFileBuildItem` [produced by the Qute extension](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/main/extensions/qute/deployment/src/main/java/io/quarkus/qute/deployment/QuteProcessor.java#L3330).

> maybe we should fill the timestampSet.watchedFileTimestamps with the resources matching the predicate at startup.

Yes, something like that. But I need to look at the code again. It's not exactly straightforward.

issue.title: Dev mode: fix HotDeploymentWatchedFileBuildItem predicate
